page: Amazon Web Services inf1.xlarge is an instance within the inf1 family, featuring AWS Inferentia Gen1 technology. It is built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz and features 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of L3 cache. It supports AVX and AVX512F instruction sets, but lacks AVX512_VNNI and AMX capabilities.

The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include any local NVMe SSD storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps. The instance does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Although designated as an Inferentia machine, the instance profile reports zero standard GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates that the inf1.xlarge exhibits weak to average performance across general compute workloads. Single-core performance is average, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1491.39 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1149.0. However, multi-core scaling is weak, as shown by a stress-ng multi-core score of 3929.66 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2526.0. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with both read and write large-block memory bandwidth falling into the bottom 25 percent, and the PassMark memory score rated as poor.

For machine learning workloads, the instance achieves an average text generation speed of 75.74 tokens per second on a small 135M LLM model, though prompt processing for the same model is weak at 225.83 tokens per second. Given the dedicated CPU allocation and specialized Inferentia silicon, this instance is tailored for entry-level machine learning inference, lightweight text processing, and basic web serving, while being less suitable for memory-intensive databases or heavy multi-threaded compilation tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services inf1.xlarge is an x86_64 virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor running at 2.5 GHz. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, it features 4 dedicated vCPUs, 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with no local storage or standard GPUs. Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities but weak multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth, with large-block memory reads and writes limited to 27.68 GB/sec and 23.83 GB/sec respectively. While general-purpose compute and database operations are weak, the instance achieves an average text generation speed of 75.74 tokens per second on small 135M LLM models. This hardware profile makes the inf1.xlarge qualitatively cost-efficient for specialized, entry-level machine learning inference and lightweight text processing workloads that leverage its dedicated CPU allocation and Inferentia architecture, rather than memory-heavy or highly parallelized general computing.
